..
Issued at 320 PM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

Early afternoon GOES-East Day Cloud Phase RGB imagery shows tranquil 
weather with only some fair weather cu over the eastern UP. Upper 
air pattern consists of primarily northwesterly flow over the north-
central CONUS as split flow at the US/Canada border at the Rockies 
is leading to high surface pressure upstream but with low pressure 
developing in the central to northern Plains. Elsewhere, a deep 
closed low continues to gyrate over Quebec with several embedded 
shortwaves. For today, the high pressure will lead to this being the 
last well above normal day (highs in the 50s are ~10 degrees above 
normal) until next week as cooler weather comes in for the later 
half of the week and into the weekend.

Tonight, the aforementioned low pressure will track south of the 
area bringing increasing cloudiness to the area. An area of rain 
will accompany this low on the north side in an area of moderate 
fgen providing forcing coinciding with deeper moisture. Models 
diverge on the exact placement of this feature but felt confident 
enough to bring PoPs up over the southern half of the U.P. late 
tonight into Wednesday morning. NBM was running cold for tonight 
with temperatures below freezing over the interior. Given the 
increasing cloud cover and rain chances, opted to blend in some raw 
(non-bias corrected) guidance to keep lows Wednesday morning above 
freezing.

While the southern branch of the upstream shortwave (and its 
associated surface low) head south of the region, the Quebec closed 
low aloft retrogrades, resulting in a series of shortwaves passing 
over the area and Wednesday through Friday. This will bring a 
sustained period of cold advection to the area with 850mb temps 
falling into the -8 to -10C range, starting Wednesday afternoon. 
Expect temperatures to start out in the 40s for the first half of 
the day but as a cold front pushes south and northerly flow 
develops, temperatures fall through the afternoon hours. Widespread 
lake effect rain showers are expected to develop on Wednesday 
afternoon over the northern part of the U.P. in response to the 
cooler temperatures over a Lake Superior that is still around 8-10 
C. As temperatures cool through the evening expect snow to mix in 
over the higher terrain with a changeover to snow elsewhere as the 
night progresses. As the low aloft wobbles over eastern North 
America, continued cold air aloft and additional embedded shortwaves 
keep LES in the forecast through Saturday morning with daytime 
temperatures (highs in the 30s) falling to near or slightly below 
average.

Several forecast challenges present themselves with this event and 
did quite a bit of deviation from the NBM (blended guidance) in the 
forecast package. NBM is struggling to handle the pattern change 
with daytime temperatures too warm and overnight lows too cold 
(trained on cool, clear nights). Warmed temperatures up quite a bit 
for Wednesday and Thursday night. NBM was indicating lows in the low 
to mid 20s over the interior with subfreezing temperatures to the 
Lake Superior shoreline. This seems unlikely given 850mb temps are 
only -8 to -10 and the lake temperatures are 8-10C. Additionally, 
widespread cloudiness and precipitation will limit cooling. Brought 
lows up to around 34 near the lakeshore and low 30s over the eastern 
U.P., with upper 20s across the west for Wednesday night. Similar 
adjustments may be necessary for Thursday night and lows beyond then 
given continued onshore flow and previously mentioned factors. As 
far as intensity and accumulations, the NBM continues to struggle 
with QPF, so blended in other guidance (probability matched mean 
guidance, other blends, etc) to bring up QPF amounts. Convergent 
flow favors at least a few more dominant bands setting up over the 
eastern half of Lake Superior with another band over the central 
part downwind of Lake Nipigon which should moisten the atmosphere. 
Models have come into better agreement with the depth of moisture 
with most indicating at least some of the DGZ is intersected along 
with inversion heights up to 8kft (possibly higher over the 
relatively warm waters of Lake Superior). Thus moderate snowfall 
rates (0.5"-1"/hr) seem likely in the more dominant bands with the 
potential for brief heavy snow bursts (1+"/hr) over the higher 
terrain of the north-central and possibly Keweenaw. Marginally cold 
low levels and warm ground temperatures will probably keep snow 
ratios on the lower side but still expecting several inches of 
snowfall over the higher terrain (Keweenaw, Marquette County and 
Baraga County) Wednesday night through Friday, with the most 
impactful period being during the overnight hours with some 
improvement during the daytime as temperatures warm close to or 
slightly above freezing. Near the lakeshore and over the eastern 
U.P. temperatures will likely remain above freezing but wouldn't be 
surprised to see accumulations in the grass
